title: Gautam Dhimal takes international productions into Nepal’s Himalayas - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Gautam Dhimal takes international productions into Nepal’s Himalayas  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Gautam Dhimal. Photo: Gautam Dhimal

Kathmandu, October 25

Filming an advertising campaign in the Himalayas involves more than finding the right mountain backdrop. Altitude, weather, access and equipment logistics can all shape how a production unfolds. For Nepali producer, photographer and visual storyteller Gautam Dhimal, these challenges have been part of a career spanning international advertising, documentary filmmaking, fashion campaigns and aerial photography.

His portfolio includes work associated with brands such as Coca-Cola, Red Bull, Panasonic, Vicks, Nippon Paint, Samsonite and Kellogg’s. One project involved a Powerade campaign by Coca-Cola Germany filmed in the high Himalayas ahead of the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

Other campaigns included Nippon Paint’s use of Kathmandu’s streets and a Panasonic project in the Himalayan region. Each required a different setting, creative approach and set of production arrangements.

For Gautam Dhimal, whose work combines visual storytelling with production management, the task extends beyond capturing an image. It also involves translating a creative brief into a shoot that can be carried out on the ground.

Behind the camera

International productions often arrive with a clear creative vision, but executing that vision in Nepal can involve coordinating multiple moving parts.

Filming in remote areas may require permits from relevant authorities, transportation for crews and equipment, accommodation, local casting and contingency plans for changing weather. Productions involving drones, helicopters or high-altitude locations can bring additional permissions and safety considerations.

Gautam Dhimal works across several aspects of this process, including line production, location coordination, aerial cinematography and photography. His experience also extends beyond Nepal, with projects in destinations including Dubai, Thailand and South Africa.

His professional biography lists collaborations with international media and entertainment organisations, including BBC One, FOX and Disney. His photography work covers advertising, fashion, editorial assignments, landscapes and wildlife.

The combination of production and photography gives him experience on both sides of a shoot, from the visual concept to the practical decisions needed to realise it.

Finding the right setting

Nepal offers filmmakers a range of locations, from Himalayan peaks and high-altitude plateaus to dense forests, rivers, traditional settlements and historic cities. For advertising agencies and filmmakers, these environments provide different ways to establish the mood and setting of a story.

A sports campaign might use the mountains to convey endurance and adventure, while a fashion shoot could draw on the contrast between dramatic landscapes and historic architecture. Kathmandu’s streets, meanwhile, offer a different visual character from the country’s remote regions.

But the appeal of these locations comes with logistical demands. Access, permits, transport and safety arrangements can affect production schedules and budgets, making local knowledge an important part of planning an international shoot.

For Nepal’s film and advertising sector, productions of this kind can also create work for local crew members, photographers, transport operators, casting professionals and other service providers.

Beyond advertising

Gautam Dhimal’s interests extend beyond commercial assignments. He also photographs wildlife, landscapes and remote environments, documenting animals, plants and ecosystems across Nepal and elsewhere.

His professional profile notes recognition from the International Photography Awards (IPA), alongside experience in aerial photography and high-altitude fashion campaigns.

Across these different forms of work, photography remains central to his practice, whether the brief involves a global brand or documenting a landscape away from an advertising set.

International productions depend on both creative direction and the ability to manage the realities of filming in unfamiliar environments. Dhimal’s career brings these elements together, spanning the visual work seen by audiences and the coordination required to produce it.

His experience also offers a glimpse into a less visible part of Nepal’s creative industry, where local professionals help international production teams turn ideas into finished campaigns.

title: Approval of Nepali projects from Adaptation Fund milestone: Minister Chaudhary - The Rising Nepal
description: Approval of Nepali projects from Adaptation Fund milestone: Minister Chaudhary  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Oct 25: Minister for Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Geeta Chaudhary, has said it is a milestone for Nepal to have its projects approved by the Adaptation Fund for the mitigation of climate-induced disaster and strengthening of adaptation capacity.

The 47th Board of Adaptation Fund had endorsed three projects which were proposed by Nepal government in a bid to strengthen capacity for better adaptation to climate change.

"At a time when the demand for financial sources for adaptation was on rise and the budget was under strain at Adaptation Fund, the approval of three projects is a huge achievement," she observed. The approval of Nepal's projects would help manage budget to cope with environmental loss.

'Green Koshi' is one of the projects receiving the fund to be utilized for conservation of the ecosystem in Koshi region through a nature-based solution. It would help build resilience too. The implementing agency is the National Nature Conservation Trust (NNCT). The financial assistance proposed for the undertaking is 9.9 million US dollars.

Also the chair of NNCT, Minister Chaudhary informed that Nepal was also receiving the assistance from other sectors.

'Strengthening Adaptation and Flood and Landside Early Warning for the Hindukush Himalaya' is the second project endorsed by the Adaptation Fund. The implementing agency for the project is ICIMOD. The amount proposed is 30 million US dollars for the enforcement of this project.

The third project is related to local level leadership and nature-based solution as a climate action in Lumbini Province. It has aimed at building resilient community. The UN Habitat is implementing the project which has proposed 4.9 million US dollars.(RSS)

title: Bay of Bengal cyclone to bring rain and snow to Nepal from Thursday night - The Kathmandu Post
description: Bay of Bengal cyclone to bring rain and snow to Nepal from Thursday night  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
A low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a powerful cyclone, bringing cloudy skies to Nepal from Wednesday and increasing the likelihood of rain from Thursday, according to the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology.

Rojan Lamichhane, a meteorologist at the department, said clouds would begin building on Wednesday, with isolated showers possible in some areas. Some Himalayan locations could also receive snowfall.

“Wednesday is expected to be cloudy, with isolated showers in some places and possible snowfall in parts of the Himalayas,” he said in the department’s weather bulletin on Sunday morning. “The system’s influence will increase on Thursday. From the afternoon, some Himalayan and hilly areas of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces could receive rain.”

The system’s effects are expected to be strongest from Thursday night through Friday and into Saturday afternoon, Lamichhane said.

Rain is forecast in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, as well as the eastern parts of Lumbini province. The impact is expected to be weaker farther west.

With the paddy harvest under way and the trekking and mountaineering season in progress, Lamichhane urged farmers and travellers to take precautions.

“Those planning to go trekking should remain alert. Trekkers and tourists in Himalayan districts need to exercise caution during this period,” he said. “Those already on the trails should move to safe locations. Since the effects are expected to be greater from Thursday to Saturday, farmers would be better off bringing in their paddy before then or waiting until the adverse weather has passed.”

Meteorologist Binod Pokharel also said several weather models were indicating a similar likelihood of rain. In an analysis shared on social media, he warned that the risk of rainfall would be comparatively high from Thursday through Saturday, including in Kathmandu and several districts across Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces.

“Clouds will begin building from Wednesday, but heavy rain is possible in most places from Thursday,” Pokharel said in a video posted on social media. While the impact is expected to be weaker in Sudurpashchim and Karnali provinces, heavy rain is possible from eastern Lumbini to Koshi province, he said.

Pokharel’s analysis identified 29 districts across five provinces as potentially at risk.

He said rainfall could intensify if the low-pressure system from the Bay of Bengal interacts with an upper-level trough as it approaches Nepal. Such conditions could damage ripe paddy still standing in fields as well as harvested crops left out to dry. He urged farmers to prepare in advance.

David Dhakal, another meteorologist at the department, said the system developing over the Bay of Bengal would also influence Nepal’s weather. Its effects could initially be felt around Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces before spreading farther west, he said. However, the amount of rainfall and the level of risk could not yet be determined with certainty.

According to the India Meteorological Department, the low-pressure system formed over the east-central Bay of Bengal and the adjoining south-eastern region is gradually strengthening. It was forecast to intensify into a deep depression on Sunday and develop into a cyclone over the west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.

The system is expected to strengthen further as it moves west-north-west, reaching waters near the Andhra Pradesh coast by Wednesday morning. It is forecast to move towards the coast of northern Andhra Pradesh and adjoining southern Odisha.

title: Nepal exports electricity worth $39 million to India a month after flash floods - The Hindu
description: Nepal exports electricity worth $39 million to India a month after flash floods  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
Nepal exported electricity worth over $39 million to India between mid-September and mid-October, according to a local media report on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) Executive Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said that electricity exports recovered during the period after being briefly disrupted by the flash floods in August.

UN climate damages fund earmarks $20 million to Nepal for August disaster

Flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche in the high Himalayas near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, killing around 1,400 people, while more than 5,000 remain missing.

Homes, vehicles, roads, bridges and hydropower projects were damaged during the floods.

"Nepal exported electricity worth approximately Nepalese Rupees 5.92 billion ($39 million approx.) to India from mid-September to mid-October," Mr. Shrestha was quoted as saying by The Himalayan Times newspaper.

Nearly two-thirds of the cross-border electricity supply to India was exported under bilateral agreements, he added.

On Friday (October 23, 2026), Nepal resumed exporting 40 megawatts of electricity to Bangladesh through India's transmission network.

The supply had been halted after the Bhotekoshi flash floods damaged the Trishuli and Chilime hydropower plants, which were designated to supply electricity to Bangladesh.

title: Three dead, three missing in motorboat accident in eastern Nepal - The Kathmandu Post
description: Three dead, three missing in motorboat accident in eastern Nepal  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Three people died, and three others went missing after a motorboat crashed at Triveni in Sangurigadhi Rural Municipality-10, Dhankuta district, on Sunday afternoon. One injured passenger is receiving treatment at Chatara Hospital.

According to the Dhankuta District Police Office, the boat, fitted with an outboard motor, was carrying 15 passengers and its operator from Kopche in Hatuwagadhi Rural Municipality-9, Bhojpur district, to Chatara in Barahakshetra, Sunsari district. The accident occurred at around 2 pm.

Preliminary reports suggest the accident was caused by brake failure. Narayan Ranjitkar, superintendent of police in Dhankuta, said police rescued 12 people, including the boat operator, and took them to Chatara Hospital for treatment.

Three people died during treatment, police said. One was identified as 52-year-old Lila Rai of Barahakshetra Municipality-1 in Sunsari. The other two were a girl aged about six and a man aged around 40. Their identities have yet to be established.

Mohan Sunar, 31, of Hatuwagadhi Rural Municipality-4 in Bhojpur, was injured in the accident. His condition is normal, and he is receiving treatment at Chatara Hospital, police said.

Some passengers managed to swim to safety, while other rescued passengers have returned home, according to police. The boat operator, Suman Magar, 24, of Barahakshetra Municipality-1, has been taken into police custody.

The three people still missing are Shivak Magar, seven, the son of Nita Magar of Kankai Municipality-4 in Jhapa; Pramila Magar, 21; and Manu Rai, 22, both from Barahakshetra Municipality-1 in Sunsari.
